newsitem.title: JAPAN: Court starts hearing Japan child killing case.
newsitem.headline: Court starts hearing Japan child killing case.

text.p: A juvenile court in Japan on Monday began hearings into the case of a 15-year-old schoolboy accused of strangling and beheading a playmate, Japanese media reported.
The hearing at Kobe Family Court in western Japan was closed to the public, and court officials have been ordered not to talk to the media about the proceedings, Kyodo news service reported.

The boy, whose name was withheld because he is a minor, was arrested on suspicion of killing and beheading 11-year-old Jun Hase in the port city of Kobe and was later charged with the murder of a 10-year-old schoolgirl and three other attacks.
The boy's lawyers requested that the suspect go through psychological tests, in which case the proceedings will be delayed for several months, Kyodo said.
Police have kept the suspect's identity under wraps because Japan's Juvenile Law says authorities must not reveal names and details of criminal suspects under 18 years of age.
The law also says that juvenile court proceedings must be closed to the public.
If the boy is found guilty of the murders he will face a maximum sentence of three years detention at a juvenile correction centre.

Media reports have said the boy has confessed to the attacks, and shown police a pond where he disposed of a hammer, a knife and a saw used to decapitate Hase, whose head was found in front of the gate to the suspect's school in May.
The weapons were recovered by police divers.
Police said the suspect wrote a note saying he carried out the attacks as a "sacred experiment" to determine the frailty of humans.
